title: axis
summary: Query or set axis limits, visibility, and aspect behavior in MATLAB and RunMat plotting.
description: `axis` queries or configures limits, visibility, and aspect behavior for the active axes. It supports four-, six-, and eight-element numeric limit vectors, target-handle queries, logical or numeric visibility controls, and command forms such as `axis equal`, `axis image`, `axis auto`, and `axis tight`.
behaviors: `axis()` returns the current x and y limits as a four-element double vector, adding z limits for a configured 3-D view. `axis(ax)` queries the specified axes.
Four-, six-, and eight-element vectors set x/y, x/y/z, or x/y/z/color limits respectively. A `-Inf` lower endpoint or `Inf` upper endpoint retains the current data-fitted endpoint.
Limit vectors accept all eight integer classes. Authoritative integer storage is validated before one deliberate conversion into host double graphics state, and later limit queries return double.
`axis('on')`, `axis('off')`, logical scalars, and numeric zero or one control axes visibility. Numeric visibility accepts all eight integer classes.
`axis equal` enables equal aspect behavior on the current axes.
`axis image` enables equal aspect behavior and returns limits to data-fitted bounds, matching MATLAB's `axis equal` plus `axis tight` behavior.
`axis auto` clears explicit limits and returns to automatic fitting.
`axis tight` uses data-driven fitting behavior while leaving figure-local plot contents unchanged.
Axis settings are subplot-local because they act on the active axes state.
GPU-resident limits and visibility controls reject before provider access because `axis` is a host graphics-state operation and exposes no interactive GPU-array input surface.
Multiple mode arguments, target-handle setter forms, mode subsets, and complete direction/style mode effects remain general graphics compatibility gaps.

gpu_support.notes: `axis` updates host-side plotting state. Numeric plot data can still use the existing GPU rendering fast paths.

gpu_residency: `axis` returns host-side limit vectors and does not change array GPU residency.
gpu_behavior: `axis` performs no provider dispatch; resident limits and visibility controls reject rather than gathering.

faqs.question: How do I get equal aspect ratio so circles look like circles?
How do I set manual axis limits?
faqs.answer: Pass a four-element vector: `axis([xmin xmax ymin ymax])`. For 3-D plots, use six elements: `axis([xmin xmax ymin ymax zmin zmax])`; append color limits for the eight-element form. Use `-Inf` for an automatic lower endpoint or `Inf` for an automatic upper endpoint. Explicit bounds override auto-fitting until you call `axis auto`.

faqs.question: What does axis tight actually do?
faqs.answer: `axis tight` fits the axes limits snugly around the plotted data with no padding. Compare to `axis auto`, which may add margin for readability. Use `tight` when you want the data to fill the entire axes area — useful for image-like plots or when whitespace is wasted space.

faqs.question: What does axis image do?
faqs.answer: `axis image` combines equal aspect behavior with data-fitted limits. It is intended for image displays where pixels should appear square and the axes should fit the image data.
